elicitation_input.question: What happened at Scapa Flow on 21st June 1919?

llm_generation.text:
On 21 June 1919, the German High Seas Fleet, which had been interned at Scapa Flow (the Royal Navy's base in Orkney, Scotland) since the Armistice of November 1918, was deliberately scuttled by its own crews.

The fleet had been interned pending the outcome of the Paris Peace Conference negotiations that would become the Treaty of Versailles. Rear Admiral Ludwig von Reuter, the German officer in command of the interned fleet, believed that negotiations had broken down (or that the armistice was about to expire) and that the ships would either be surrendered permanently to the Allies or seized. To prevent this, he secretly gave the order for the fleet to be scuttled.

German sailors opened seacocks and watertight doors throughout the ships, and over the course of the day 52 of the 74 interned vessels sank, including battleships and battlecruisers. British guard ships attempted to stop the sinkings, boarding some vessels and even opening fire on German sailors attempting to abandon ship—nine German sailors were killed, the last casualties of World War I.

Most of the sunken ships were later salvaged during the 1920s and 1930s for scrap, though a handful remain on the seabed at Scapa Flow to this day and are popular sites for recreational diving.
